newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOTOR RACING-FORMER F1 DRIVERS TO RACE FOR NISSAN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FORMER F1 DRIVERS TO RACE FOR NISSAN.

text.p: Six former Formula One drivers will drive Nissan Motor Co's new GT car in the Le Mans 24-hour sportscar race in France next June, the firm said on Wednesday.
The drivers are Riccard Patrese, Martin Brundle, Gianni Morbidelli, Aguri Suzuki, Eric van de Poele, and Erik Comas, Nissan said.

Other drivers for Nissan are Jorg Muller, now a test driver for the F1 racing team Arrows Grand Prix International; Kazuyoshi Hoshino, a racing driver dubbed the man fastest in Japan; and Masahiko Kageyama, the 1995 champion on Japanese GT car championship.
"I am confident (Nissan can win at Le Mans). We developed our strongest racing vehicles and engines ever," Nissan president Yoshikazu Hanawa told Reuters.
"If we win, it will help raise our car market share and boost the morale of our employees."

The new car, the Nissan R390 GT1, is a "C" category car powered by a Nissan-developed 3.5-litre twin-turbo V-8 engine and was jointly developed with the British Automotive engineering company Tom Walkinshaw Racing (TWR) group.
TWR, which runs the F1 racing team Arrows Grand Prix International, develops racing cars in collaboration with Volvo and Jaguar.
Nissan would start selling the sports car this autumn with a price tag of about 100 million yen ($813,000), Hanawa said. "We have already received inquiries for the car," he said.
Three of the new cars would take part in the GT1 category of the Le Mans 24-hour endurance race, which begins on June 14, he said.
The car features a carbon-fibre monocoque body and a six-speed sequential gearbox. It will be equipped with an anti-lock brake system and transaction control system.

"We achieved better results than expected on a shakedown test of the race car in Estril, Portugal, on March 13," said Yutaka Hagiwara, general manager of Nissan's motorsports planning and development centre. ($1=123 yen)
